# D-0066 — Outbound SMS to leads: TCPA-compliant consent language

**Date:** 2026-07-28
**Status:** RATIFIED 2026-07-28 (companion to D-0064)
**Author:** Claude Code (with steward)
**Scope:** All outbound SMS to leads generated by Mission 1 forms. Affects `apps/web/src/app/contact/ContactForm.tsx`, the new `/pet-waste` landing page form, the `/quote` calculator, and any other lead-capture form.
**Review date:** 2026-08-28 (30 days post-launch or post-1st-paid-customer, whichever first)
**Confidence (shipped):** 0.85
**Supersedes:** none (first formal SMS-consent ratification)

---

## 0. The decision in one paragraph

Ratify the **TCPA-compliant SMS consent language** required at the point of form submission before any outbound SMS is sent to a lead:

> **"I agree to receive SMS messages from Largo Lawn at the number provided. Message frequency varies. Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help. Message and data rates may apply."**

This language is presented as a **required checkbox** immediately above the submit button on every lead-capture form. The checkbox state is captured in the form payload and persisted with the lead record. The acknowledgement SMS (and any follow-up SMS) is sent **only if the checkbox is checked**.

---

## 1. Problem

The GTM drafts (`output/gtm/02-tracking-stack-spec.md`) propose sending an acknowledgement SMS to every lead who provides a phone number, with no explicit consent capture. The current `apps/web/src/app/contact/ContactForm.tsx` has no consent checkbox and no consent language. Sending SMS to leads without explicit consent violates the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) and risks:

- **Carrier filtering** (A2P 10DLC registration requirement; carriers reject unconsented traffic).
- **TCPA private right of action** ($500-$1,500 per unsolicited message).
- **Brand and trust damage** if a complaint is filed with the FCC or state attorney general.

The steward explicitly chose the recommended standard-consent option on 2026-07-28.

---

## 2. Context

What we know:

- TCPA requires "prior express written consent" for marketing SMS and "prior express consent" for informational/transactional SMS.
- Carriers (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile) operate under CTIA guidelines and A2P 10DLC registration rules; unconsented SMS is filtered or rejected.
- The current privacy page (`apps/web/src/app/privacy/page.tsx`) does not mention SMS; it must be updated to disclose SMS as a contact channel once consent is captured.
- The existing acknowledgement flow uses `sendLeadResponse` from `@grass/notifications-core` (currently email + SMS via personal phone per the privacy page). Stage 2 of the plan (D-0064 §11) will formalize this.

What we explicitly don't know:

- Whether the existing SMS-sending path is on a 10DLC-registered long code or a personal number. If personal, this must be addressed before any production SMS is sent.

---

## 3. Requirements

A successful ratification must:

1. Add a **required checkbox** to every lead-capture form (ContactForm, /pet-waste page form, /quote calculator) with the consent language in §0.
2. Capture the checkbox state (`sms_consent: boolean`) in the form payload.
3. Persist `sms_consent` with the lead record in the CRM.
4. Send the acknowledgement SMS only if `sms_consent === true`.
5. Honor STOP and HELP keywords at any time after consent is given; persistent opt-out state must be queryable from the lead record.
6. Update `apps/web/src/app/privacy/page.tsx` to disclose SMS as a contact channel and to disclose the consent capture mechanism.
7. Document the SMS-sending path (10DLC-registered long code vs. personal number) before any production SMS is sent.

---

## 4. Alternatives considered

| Option | Approach | Pro | Con | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | **This ADR** — required TCPA-compliant checkbox before any SMS | Legally defensible; carrier-friendly | One extra click per form submission | **Selected** |
| B | Implied consent (no checkbox, rely on existing form language) | Faster to ship | Legally weaker; carrier filtering risk | **Rejected** |
| C | No SMS for pilot — email only | Removes SMS question entirely | Loses speed-to-lead advantage | **Rejected** |
| D | Double opt-in (send confirmation SMS, require reply YES) | Strongest consent | Two-message overhead; delays acknowledgement | **Considered** — not selected for pilot (single opt-in with clear STOP/HELP is industry-standard for local-service transactional SMS) |

---

## 5. Evaluation matrix

| Criterion | A (this ADR) | B (implied) | C (no SMS) | D (double opt-in) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Legal defensibility (TCPA) | ✓ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓✓ |
| Carrier acceptance (A2P 10DLC) | ✓ | ✗ | n/a | ✓ |
| Conversion friction | low (one click) | none | none | medium (two messages) |
| Acknowledgement speed | fast | fast | slow (email only) | medium |
| Operational complexity | low | lowest | lowest | medium |

---

## 6. Decision

**Selected: Option A.** Add a required TCPA-compliant checkbox to every lead-capture form. Capture and persist consent with the lead record. Send SMS only when consent is true. Honor STOP/HELP keywords. Update privacy page.

---

## 7. Risk register additions

| Risk ID | Title | Likelihood | Impact | Score | Owner | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-SMS-001 | Lead submits form but forgets to check the box (lost SMS acknowledgement) | 3 (possible) | 2 (minor) | 6 | marketing | Default unchecked is correct; lead still receives email acknowledgement. Copy on form makes the consequence of unchecking clear. |
| R-SMS-002 | SMS-sending path is not 10DLC-registered | 4 (likely if not addressed) | 4 (major) | 16 | operations | Audit the SMS-sending path before Stage 2 ships. If un-registered, register the long code or migrate to a 10DLC-compliant provider. |
| R-SMS-003 | STOP/HELP handling fails (lead keeps receiving SMS after opt-out) | 2 (unlikely) | 5 (catastrophic) | 10 | operations | STOP/HELP handling is built into the SMS provider's standard; test before production. |
| R-SMS-004 | Privacy page not updated; consent capture is non-compliant on paper | 2 (unlikely) | 4 (major) | 8 | compliance | Privacy page update is a Stage 0 deliverable alongside this ADR. |

---

## 8. Rollback

Rollback is staged and reversible:

1. **Disable the checkbox** in the form (revert to no-checkbox state). All lead-capture reverts to email-only acknowledgement.
2. **Revert SMS sending** in the lead API route (skip SMS even when checkbox was checked).
3. **Revert privacy page** to pre-pilot state.

Each rollback step is independently executable.

---

## 9. Form payload contract change

The `LeadInput` interface in `apps/web/src/app/api/lead/route.ts` gains one new field:

```ts
interface LeadInput {
  // ... existing fields ...
  sms_consent?: boolean;
}
```

Default: `false`. If `false`, no acknowledgement SMS is sent (email-only acknowledgement path).

The persisted lead record gains one new column:

```yaml
sms_consent: boolean  # captured at submission time, immutable thereafter
```
